key_insight: Flexible modular robots combine movement and object manipulation in a single unit. By physically connecting, they form task-adaptive structures that cooperate to carry objects, cross gaps and traverse challenging terrain.
problem_solved: Robots with fixed shapes can struggle when tasks demand different combinations of mobility, manipulation and teamwork. This work addresses the need for robotic systems that can physically adapt to changing tasks and environments.
method: Use flexible, tensegrity-based continuum robot modules that support both locomotion and manipulation.
Physically connect modules into cooperative structures with task-adaptive shapes.
Demonstrate collective capabilities through object carrying, gap crossing and navigation over challenging terrain.
impact: For AI and robotics practitioners, this work highlights physical configuration as an additional dimension of adaptive behavior. It offers a platform for exploring control and coordination across robots whose bodies and connections can change with the task.
visual_elements: Annotated module diagram highlighting its flexible tensegrity structure and movement capabilities.
Assembly sequence showing individual modules connecting into different cooperative shapes.
Three-panel task illustration: carrying an object, bridging a gap and traversing uneven terrain.
Task-to-shape map linking each challenge to a corresponding robot configuration.
paper_title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
paper_authors: Mahmud Hasan Saikot, Sydney Spiegel, Sudheera Akalanka Kariyawasam, Andrew Stefka, Josh Chrisler
